title: Score-based Greedy Search for Structure Identification of Partially Observed Causal Models
claim: Without structural assumptions, the set of algebraically equivalent latent structures is large and uninformative, so the true structure cannot be pinned down.
layout: Single layered DAG, top-down, latent nodes above shaded observed leaves
description: A single top-down directed graph. Four tiers of nodes are linked by thin black arrows. White circles are latent variables L1 to L7, and grey-blue shaded circles are observed variables X1 to X18. L1 and L2 sit at the top. L1 points to X1, X2, X3, X4, L3, L6 and L7. L2 points to L3, X4, X5 and X6. L3 sits in the second tier and points to L4, L5, L6, L7 and X7 to X9. L4 and L5 point to X10 to X14. L6 and L7 point to X14 to X18. The many crossing edges make a dense hierarchical latent structure. This is panel (a), the ground-truth graph G*. The eye goes first to the L1 and L2 roots, then follows the fan of arrows down to the observed leaves. The figure has no color contrast beyond white versus grey fill.
caption: Without further graphical assumption, the algebraic equivalence class is very large and not very informative: suppose the ground truth $\graph^*$ in (a), by [ref] we may arrive at either $\hat{\graph}_1$ (b) or $\hat{\graph}_2$ (c), both are algebraically equivalent to $\graph^*$.
abstract: Identifying the structure of a partially observed causal system is essential to various scientific fields. Recent advances have focused on constraint-based causal discovery to solve this problem, and yet in practice these methods often face challenges related to multiple testing and error propagation. These issues could be mitigated by a score-based method and thus it has raised great attention whether there exists a score-based greedy search method that can handle the partially observed scenario. In this work, we propose the first score-based greedy search method for the identification of structure involving latent variables with identifiability guarantees. Specifically, we propose Generalized N Factor Model and establish the global consistency: the true structure including latent variables can be identified up to the Markov equivalence class by using score. We then design Latent variable Greedy Equivalence Search (LGES), a greedy search algorithm for this class of model with well-defined operators, which search very efficiently over the graph space to find the optimal structure. Our experiments on both synthetic and real-life data validate the effectiveness of our method (code will be publicly available).
